prompt:
Use case: background-extraction.
Edit the supplied isometric research illustration for seamless placement directly on an existing deep navy website background.
CRITICAL: produce a genuinely transparent RGBA image with an alpha channel. The page behind it is dark blue (#081426 to #0c223c). This must be an isolated scene, not a rectangular light panel.
Preserve the existing illustration's electric car, precise body shape, wheel geometry, roof lidar, robot arm, gripper, blocks, isometric viewpoint, positions, relative sizes, blue-gray line-art style, and overall 4:3 composition. Do not replace or redesign these subjects. Keep the car and robotic arm bright and crisp enough to read on navy. Keep the light background building as delicate cool-blue architectural outlines, and the small trees as subtle semi-transparent blue silhouettes.
Remove the entire off-white paper background, white courtyard paving, ground tiles, broad pale gray ground plane and all blank background pixels. Remove any rectangular slab behind the scene. Everything between and around the subjects must be real transparency.
Retain only the car, its soft localized transparent contact shadow, the arm and its small physical workbench/base, the faint background architecture/foliage, the dotted planning path, and the two perception arcs. Render the path and sensing arcs in muted icy blue with translucent fill so the navy webpage can show through them, not opaque white. Keep architectural lines subtle rather than a big pale mass. Peripheral tree and architectural linework should softly fade to true alpha near the outside edges; there must be no bright rectangular edge, white halo, white glow, border or card around the illustration.
No text, no labels, no caption, no logo, no watermark, no figure numbering. Do not include or paint the navy webpage itself. Do not fake transparency with a checkerboard; return actual transparent pixels. Maintain a polished, restrained scientific editorial illustration.
